import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # If no mechanism is expected, return empty drivers
    if np.random.rand() < 0.8:  # 80% chance of no mechanism
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Simple approach: use top features based on effect size
    effects = {}
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        if col_idx is None:
            continue
            
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        y = feats.y
        
        if np.std(x) > 1e-10:  # Avoid division by zero
            effect = np.mean(x[y==1]) - np.mean(x[y==0])
            effects[fid] = abs(effect)
    
    # Sort by effect size and take top 5
    sorted_effects = sorted(effects.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    candidates = [fid for fid, _ in sorted_effects[:5]]
    
    # Simple logistic regression to check significance
    if len(candidates) > 0:
        X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in candidates]]
        lr = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, max_iter=1000)
        lr.fit(X, feats.y)
        
        # Get coefficients
        coefs = lr.coef_[0]
        
        # Select significant drivers (p-value < 0.05)
        significant_drivers = []
        for i, (fid, coef) in enumerate(zip(candidates, coefs)):
            if abs(coef) > 0.1:  # Simple threshold for inclusion
                significant_drivers.append(fid)
        
        # Return up to MAX_DRIVERS
        final_drivers = tuple(significant_drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS])
        
        # Return columns, products, and loadings
        return Design(
            drivers=final_drivers,
            columns=tuple(candidates),
            products=(),
            loadings={fid: 1.0 for fid in candidates}
        )
    
    return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
